one_month_reasoning: Inside the window (to 2026-10-31): a September production update in mid-October (only infrastructure reporting moved to quarterly, src 3), possible Tydal project-financing or LC-backstop headlines ahead of the 2026-12-31 Phase 1 date (src 21), ATM use (only $8.4M used by 9/29, src 22, so the overhang is latent rather than active), and BTC (~$85.4k, src 23). Q3 results (~mid-November) fall outside the window. None of these has a clear expected sign, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal around a $10.52 median (tiny negative tilt for dilution risk) at ~30% monthly sigma (108%/3.5). Round 4: the site-by-site rebuild and split discount rates change long-dated value, not what can happen in four weeks; the one dated item that matters (A201 >70% commitments, src 32) was public on 9/29, before the 10/01 close, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged (within 0.01 of the supervisor's).

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site DCF ($5.19 at Oct-2027 = 65% rising-BTC path $6.66 + 35% flat-$85k BTC $2.47; split discount rates: Tydal LC-covered rent 7.0%, rest of Tydal's firm 10-yr term 9.5%, signed GPU offtakes 11.0%, everything uncontracted/pipeline/terminal at 12.5% WACC; single-rate equivalent $4.25), a SOTP that swaps the DCF's probability-weighted power sites for market $/MW option values ($8.18), and EV/sales (2.5x ~$2.33B NTM revenue = $11.54), weighted 45/35/20 = $7.51. Every one of the 20 inventory sites appears once (see site_coverage).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site FCFF, valued at 2026-10-01 and rolled 12 months at the 15.3% cost of equity (x1.153); net debt $1.40B, 272.6M shares, 2032 notes as debt, no ATM issuance. EV components (split-rate, rising-BTC path, $M / $ per share at Oct-2027): Tydal P1-2 $1,006M / $4.25 (16-yr lease, yr-1 $233M +3%, 90% NOI, 15% tax, single phase from 2027-04-01, 10% Volta default leg in lease yr 7 with 70% re-let at 80% rent, 30% walk at yr 10, less $500M capex; lease yrs 1-5 (cumulative rent ~$1.24B, inside the ~$1.3B LCs) at 7.0%, yrs 6-10 at 9.5%, yrs 11-16 at 12.5%); A102 $315M / $1.33 ($160M/yr 2027-31, 65% EBITDA, $232M GPU capex in Q4-26, 50% prepay received up front and taken out of contract cash evenly, contract years at 11.0%, then 40% tail -15%/yr and refresh chain at WACC); A201 $786M / $3.32 (95% x the committed >70% of 21.7 MW at $340M/yr for 5 yrs from Q2-27 on 70% of the $530M rack capex; remaining 6.5 MW 60% contracted later at the same $/MW (WACC) else spot at 45%->25% of contract price; 5% failure leg puts the committed racks on the spot path); A101 $74M / $0.31 (2.5 MW, ~$42M/yr of the $86M ARR contracted to end-2029, 60% EBITDA, then tail); legacy uncontracted fleet $43M / $0.18 (~$44M ARR decaying); A202 $475M / $2.01 (risked GPU cloud: 45% contracted by RFS at 85% of A102 $/MW = $932M/yr, 60% EBITDA after the facility fee, $1.59B GPU capex 50% prepaid; 27.5% contracted from 2029 at 70% pricing after ~1.25 yrs of idle facility fee; 27.5% never contracted, paying the ~$86M/yr fee for 10 yrs less 30% sublet; all at WACC; chain truncated at the facility's 2037 end); mining (Rockdale 563, Molde 84, Gedu 100, Jigmeling 500, Oromia 50, Massillon 174+47 MW) $812M / $3.43 (FCF $172M/11M/51M/82M/100M 2027-31, g 1.5%); corporate (SEALMINER R&D + non-mining overhead, G&A assumed inside the CoinShares cash cost) -$805M / -$3.41; Sparks plant capex -$19M / -$0.08; probability-weighted pipeline $289M / $1.22 (Tydal P3 50% $139M, Knoxville 35% $62M, Wenatchee 25% $8M, Rockdale conversion 25% $59M net of displaced mining, Molde 10% $19M, Clarington 15% and Weathersfield 20% ~$1M each, Fox Creek and Gelephu $0). EV $2.98B - $1.40B = $1.58B -> $5.78 today, $6.66 at Oct-2027. Flat BTC $85k (mining TV floored at zero, i.e. rigs curtailed): $2.47. Central DCF weights the two 65/35 = $5.19. All at one 12.5% WACC: $5.72 rising / $1.52 flat / $4.25 weighted. Sensitivities (split, rising BTC): refresh at 60% / 100% of today's revenue per $ capex $4.94 / $8.38; life 5y $6.36, 7y $6.72; WACC 11%/g1.5% $8.43, 14%/g0% $4.92; contracted rates +/-1pt $6.34-$6.83; A202 contract probability 30% / 60% -> A202 $354M / $597M.

inputs_detail.input: Tydal P1-2 rent, start and default leg
inputs_detail.value: yr-1 $233M +3%/yr, 90% NOI, single phase from 2027-04-01; 10% default in lease yr 7, 30% walk at yr 10
inputs_detail.derivation: $4.7B/16 yrs with 3% escalators gives yr-1 $233M (src 21). Start: I keep the CEO's Q2-call 'one phase at the Phase-2 date' (src 31) over the written Dec-26/Mar-27 phases (src 21, src 36 flag 12) because it is the most recent management statement; the written dates would add ~$29M. Default leg added (sites flag 13): the reported end-customer deal behind Volta runs ~6 yrs, shorter than the 10-yr firm term, and the ~$1.3B LCs are still 'anticipated', so 10% default at yr 7, 18 months dark, 70% re-let at 80% rent.

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate: Tydal LC-covered rent (lease yrs 1-5)
inputs_detail.derivation: Cumulative rent in yrs 1-5 (~$1.24B) sits inside the ~$1.3B of LCs arranged by J.P. Morgan affiliates and another top-tier bank (src 21, src 36 contracts_credit), so these flows carry bank (AA-range) credit plus completion/operating risk: 10y UST 5.29% (src 12) + ~1.0pt bank credit + ~0.7pt completion/operating and conditionality (LCs not yet issued). No contract-level debt is priced yet; Bitdeer's only priced secured debt (BIT asset loan, 13.0% effective) is related-party and rig-collateralised, so it is not a fair anchor for an LC-backed lease.

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate: Tydal unbacked firm term (lease yrs 6-10)
inputs_detail.derivation: Volta is private and unrated; credit sits on Volta and an unrated AI-lab end customer. 5.29% + ~4.2pt (single-B/BB single-tenant lease spread incl. operating risk) - between the LC rate and the 12.5% WACC. Years 11-16 are cancellable without fee (src 21), so they are not firm contract cash flows and stay at WACC.

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate: signed GPU offtakes (A101, A102, A201 committed)
inputs_detail.derivation: Counterparties undisclosed and unrated (src 36 contracts_credit), so not investment-grade; prepayments covering ~50% of capex (src 3) cut the capital at risk, and terms are short (5 yrs), but Bitdeer carries GPU uptime/operating risk. Set between the 9.5% unbacked-lease rate and the 12.5% WACC, below the 13.0% related-party secured loan.

>$800M over 5 yrs, revenue from Q1-27 (src 3). Capex 9.5 MW x ~$24.4M/MW (A201's 133 racks ~$530M / 21.7 MW, src 3). Prepay ~50% of capex received at energization and counted once inside the TCV; both the capex and the prepay are assumed to fall after 9/30 so neither sits in my 9/30 net debt (supervisor's question).

inputs_detail.value: 95% x $340M/yr x 5 yrs from Q2-27 on the committed >70%; remainder 60% at the same $/MW
inputs_detail.derivation: >70% of 21.7 MW committed, >$1.7B over 5 yrs (src 32; ~$340M/yr). The release calls these 'off-take commitments' without saying executed, so 95% not 100%. Remainder 6.5 MW: 60% contracted by mid-27 (Bitdeer filled A102 and 70% of A201 within weeks), else rented spot at 45% then 25% of contract price. Capex $530M for 133 racks, a count I verified in the Aug-2026 6-K (src 3), which resolves the inventory's 128 vs >100 conflict.

inputs_detail.value: A101 ~$42M/yr contracted to end-2029 at 60% EBITDA; rest of ARR ~$44M decaying $35M->$22M at 30-35%
inputs_detail.derivation: Aug-26 6-K lists A101 (2.5 IT MW, GB200/GB300) as 100% long-term contracted and the fleet ARR as ~$86M of contractually obligated orders (src 3). A101's share is sized at A102's ~$16.8M/MW = ~$42M (term not disclosed; 3 yrs assumed); the rest (H100/H200/B200) is treated as uncontracted on the round-3 decay path (src 25, 26), so the two rows do not overlap.

inputs_detail.value: 45% contracted by RFS at 85% of A102 $/MW; 27.5% from 2029 at 70%; 27.5% never; facility fee ~$86M/yr for 10 yrs
inputs_detail.derivation: Bitdeer is the customer under a 10-yr services agreement and had no offtake (src 33); management expects A102-like per-MW economics (src 33), which I haircut 15% for 2027-28 Vera Rubin pricing in a supply-long market (src 24). Fee is undisclosed: ~$110/kW-month ex-power x 65.1 MW, ~55% of the US primary-market average $196 (src 34) for lower-cost Johor - judgment. GPU capex $1.59B (65.1 x $24.4M/MW), 50% prepaid. 45% by RFS reflects A102's sell-out and A201's 70% in two weeks, but A202 is 3x A201 and needs ~$0.8B of net funding. All at WACC (uncontracted). Supervisor range was $0.1-0.4B; mine is $0.48B because the contracted leg keeps the round-3 refresh economics.

inputs_detail.input: GPU life, tail and refresh (all GPU sites)
inputs_detail.value: 6-yr economic life; tail 40% of contract price -15%/yr; refresh at 80% of today's 0.69x revenue/capex, 65% EBITDA, 50% prepaid
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 3. Company lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (since Jan-2026), IREN 5 (src 35; round 3 wrongly had IREN at 6). Contract term is 5 yrs, plus one cash-positive tail year. Refresh revenue/capex is now a fixed 0.69 x 80% for every site (round 3 used A102/A201's blend), so A201's richer signed pricing is not carried into refresh.

Round-3 path (Aug run-rate 1,310 BTC/month, src 3, trimmed for network growth; halving Apr-2028, src 19; Polymarket odds, src 8, 9). Massillon's 21+26 MW rebuild is insurance funded (src 36) and lifts output and cost ~2%. Fox Creek (101 MW, Q4-27) is not added to output: at post-halving economics its rigs and plant capex do not pay back.
CoinShares Q2-2026 Bitdeer cash cost $61.1k/BTC ex-tax (src 7) x volume; capex against $202.6M H1-2026 D&A (src 4).

Supervisor: G&A is probably already inside CoinShares' cash cost (src 37), so I drop ~$60M/yr of G&A and keep SEALMINER R&D (~$11.3k/BTC = ~$110M in 2027, cut to ~$60M after the halving, src 7) plus ~$30M/yr of AI/HPC overhead that the mining cash cost cannot contain.

inputs_detail.value: Tydal P3 50%, Knoxville 35%, Wenatchee 25%, Rockdale 25%, Molde 10%, Clarington 15%, Weathersfield 20%; rent $1.8-1.93M/IT MW +3%, 90% NOI, 15 yrs; capex $4.1M (Tydal) to $10M/IT MW (greenfield Ohio)
inputs_detail.derivation: Each valued as a colocation lease at WACC, net of build capex and start lags: Tydal P3 sits beside a signed campus (2H-27, self-owned); Knoxville/Wenatchee are conversions with RFS slipping (Q4-26 -> Oct/Dec-27); Rockdale has $100M of land bought but management only prepares AI 'in the background' (src 31) and the lost mining FCF on ~150 MW is deducted; Clarington is in litigation (motion to dismiss denied); Weathersfield RFS Q4-28. Rent from Tydal's yr-1 $1.93M/IT MW (src 21).

inputs_detail.input: WACC / cost of equity / terminal growth
inputs_detail.derivation: Ke = 5.29% (src 12) + beta 2.0 x 5% ERP (beta judged from 108-119% realized vol, src 15) = 15.3%; pre-tax debt ~6.5% blended (5% converts, 13% BIT asset loan, 3% BTC loan, src 22); ~59/41 equity/debt at market -> 11.7%, +0.8pt for BTC/execution risk. Terminal growth applies only to mining + corporate; GPU sites use explicit cohorts and leases are finite.
227.4M Class A + 44.4M Class V at 6/30 (src 4) + 767,199 ATM shares to 9/29 (src 22). 2032 notes held as debt.

As round 3: gross debt ~$1.98B at face less ~$0.55-0.6B liquid assets (src 22). A201 rack payments are modelled as future capex; if some were paid in Q3 they are counted twice (up to ~$0.7/sh conservative).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Same split-rate site values as the DCF for contracted and GPU sites (Tydal $1,006M, A102 $315M, A201 $786M, A101 $74M, legacy $43M, A202 $475M), mining $812M, corporate -$805M, Sparks -$19M = $2.69B; plus power optionality at market $/MW, incremental to mining and counted once per MW: Rockdale 742 MW x $0.4M = $297M, Massillon 221 x $0.2M = $44M, Molde 84 x $0.2M = $17M, Weathersfield 300 x $0.25M = $75M, Clarington 570 x $0.1M = $57M (litigation), Fox Creek 101 x $0.1M = $10M, Gelephu $0, Bhutan/Ethiopia 650 MW $0 (no HPC market); AI pipeline Tydal P3 / Knoxville / Wenatchee at their DCF values ($209M) = $0.71B. EV $3.40B - net debt $1.40B = $2.00B / 272.6M = $7.32 today, x1.118 = $8.18.

inputs_detail.derivation: From the DCF leg (split rates).
From the DCF leg; corporate excludes G&A assumed inside the CoinShares cash cost.

inputs_detail.value: $0.1-0.4M/MW on US/Norway sites; $0 for Bhutan, Ethiopia and the Gelephu LOI
inputs_detail.derivation: CoinShares: unleased energized capacity at listed miners trades below $3M/MW (src 7). I give Rockdale ~one-seventh of that (land bought, no tenant), Massillon/Molde/Weathersfield $0.2-0.25M, and litigated or gas-dependent sites $0.1M. These replace (not add to) the DCF's probability-weighted values for the same sites.
As DCF.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct-2027 ~$2.33B (Tydal $237M, A101 $42M, legacy $30M, A102 $160M, A201 $437M expected, A202 $419M risked (45% x $932M), mining ~$1.0B with the halving inside the window) x 2.5x = $5.81B EV - projected net debt ~$2.2B = $3.61B / ~313M shares = ~$11.5.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3's $1.87B less A202 colocation ($117M) plus A202 risked GPU revenue ($419M), A201 at 95% x $340M + remainder ($437M vs $219M) and Massillon +2%.

CoinShares: BTDR 2.9x vs 3.7x pure miners and 12.9x HPC-contracted peers (src 7); cut from 3.0x to 2.5x because the halving falls inside the NTM window (supervisor point) and the sales mix is still ~60% mining.
Round 3's $1.8B + ~$0.36B expected A202 net capex (45% x $1.59B less 50% prepay) + ~$0.1B more A201 capex (all 133 racks, not 60%) - ~$0.06B lower corporate cost.
~273M (src 22) + ~40M from ~$0.4B of the $1B ATM (src 16, 22) at ~$10.

bear.story: BTC follows the cycle script to a sub-$60k trough (Polymarket ~14% for <$60k before 2027, src 8), A202 stays empty while Bitdeer pays its 10-yr facility fee, Tydal's LCs or project debt slip, and equity is issued under the $1B ATM at low prices. At ~$4-5 the equity is roughly contracted site value (Tydal + A101/A102/A201 ~$2.2B at split rates) less $1.4B net debt; the flat-BTC DCF ($2.5) is the floor-ish reference.

base.story: BTC $80-100k; Tydal commences Q1-27, A102 and A201 bill from Q1/Q2-27, A202 gets partly contracted around RFS; ~15% dilution and the 2028 halving cap the multiple. Up from $9.3: A201's commitments and a full site count lift contracted value, but the 9/29 news was already in the 10/01 close, so only part of the fair-value change carries through.

bull.story: A202 fills at A102-like pricing, a second large lease at Rockdale or Ohio is signed (power sites at peer $/MW, src 7, 17, 20) and BTC recovers after the trough (src 19). Tydal's contracted cash flows at a 7-9.5% rate plus GPU backlog ~$2.9B re-rate BTDR toward contracted peers.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$5.00 the market cap (~$1.36B) is about equal to my contracted site value (Tydal $1.01B + A101/A102/A201 $1.18B at split rates = $2.19B) less $1.40B net debt plus a little, so the market would be giving almost nothing for mining, A202, the pipeline or ~3 GW of power. Reaching it would most likely take a Tydal/Volta LC or financing failure, A202 left empty with its facility fee running, a squeeze on the 13% BIT loans, or a deep-discount equity raise - not ordinary BTC-beta volatility. Kept at $5.0 (the supervisor's level); the flat-BTC DCF ($2.5) shows it is not a floor.

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF site by site so each of the 20 inventory sites (src 36) appears once. Fixes to flags on my model: A202 is now what it is - Bitdeer pays a 10-yr facility fee and has no offtake (src 33) - so its round-3 colocation annuity and $0.80B terminal value are gone and it is a risked GPU-cloud build (45%/27.5%/27.5% legs, ~$1.59B GPU capex, ~$86M/yr fee) worth $0.48B; A201 reflects the 9/29 commitments (95% x >70% at ~$340M/yr, remainder risked, src 32); Tydal P3, Knoxville, Wenatchee, Rockdale conversion (net of displaced mining), Molde, Clarington, Weathersfield, Fox Creek and Gelephu each carry a stated probability and are valued net of build capex; Massillon's rebuild is in mining output; Tydal now has a 10% default leg. I also applied the round-3 supervisor's corrections: G&A taken out of corporate cost because CoinShares' cash cost already holds it (+~$2/sh), A102's prepay explicitly counted once, flat-BTC shown next to the rising path. Discounting is split: Tydal rent inside the LC cover at 7.0%, the rest of its firm 10-yr term at 9.5%, signed GPU offtakes at 11.0% (unrated counterparties, ~50% prepaid), everything else at the 12.5% WACC. No contract-level debt is priced yet, and the 13% BIT loan is related-party and rig-collateralised, so the contracted rates are built from the 5.29% 10y UST plus credit and completion spreads. Results at Oct-2027: rising-BTC DCF $6.66 split vs $5.72 single rate (Tydal $1.01B vs $0.82B); flat BTC $2.47 vs $1.52; central DCF (65/35) $5.19 vs $4.25, against round 3's $1.29 (supervisor-corrected ~-$0.4). Approximate bridge from the supervisor-corrected -$0.4 to the $5.72 single-rate rising-BTC DCF: G&A fix ~+$2.0, A201 commitments and full-site racks ~+$1.5, A202 as risked GPU cloud +$2.0, pipeline +$1.2, Tydal moved from round 3's 9% to the single 12.5% with a default leg -$1.3, other items (A101 carve-out, Massillon, fixed refresh ratio) ~+$0.3; split rates then add +$0.94 to $6.66, and the 35% flat-BTC weight takes the central case to $5.19. SOTP $8.18 (market $/MW options in place of the DCF's probability-weighted power sites) and EV/sales $11.5 (A202 risked revenue added, net debt for its capex). I raise the DCF weight to 45% because it now covers every site: fair value $7.51 (from $5.38), ~29% below spot. The 12-month distribution moves only partly, because the 9/29 A201 news was in the 10/01 price and most of the change is model correction: bear 28% ~$4.3, base 50% ~$9.5, bull 22% ~$18.5 (median ~$9.09, mean ~$11.50); P(>=spot) 0.367 -> 0.397. 1-month ladder and $5.0 thesis break unchanged. Research: two company releases (A201, A202), the Aug-2026 6-K re-read (133 racks), one colocation-pricing source; 1 web search.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted A101/A102/A201 revenue at contract price for the term (A102/A201 5 yrs, A101 to 2029); then 40% of contract price in the tail year, -15%/yr; cash cost ~20% of contract revenue. Refresh every 6 yrs at 80% of 0.69x revenue per $ capex, 65% EBITDA, 50% prepaid. A202 (if contracted) the same, at 85% of A102 pricing and 60% EBITDA after the facility fee, chain stopped at the 2037 facility end. Uncontracted legacy fleet -20%/yr for 2 yrs then -8%/yr.
gpu_life.note: Life values are the split-rate, rising-BTC DCF at Oct-2027 (central 65/35 BTC-weighted DCF is $5.19). The 5/6/7-yr spread ($6.36-$6.72) stays small; refresh pricing matters more ($4.94 at 60%, $8.38 at 100%). Company lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5. Tydal (tenant-owned GPUs) is outside the GPU-life logic apart from its default and walk legs.

discounting.basis: Tiered. 7.0% for Tydal rent inside the ~$1.3B LC cover (lease yrs 1-5): 10y UST 5.29% + ~1.0pt AA-range bank credit + ~0.7pt completion/operating and conditionality. 9.5% for Tydal yrs 6-10 (firm term, unrated Volta/AI-lab credit). 11.0% for signed GPU offtakes (A101, A102, A201 committed): unrated, undisclosed customers, ~50% prepaid, 5-yr terms, Bitdeer carries uptime risk. 12.5% WACC for Tydal yrs 11-16 (cancellable), A202, all pipeline, tails, refresh cohorts, mining and terminal. No contract-level debt is priced yet (Tydal project debt and A201 contract-secured financing are planned); Bitdeer's only priced secured loan (BIT asset loan, 13.0% effective) is related-party and rig-collateralised, so it caps rather than anchors the contracted rates. DCFs are per share at Oct-2027, central = 65% rising-BTC / 35% flat-BTC: split $5.19 (rising $6.66, flat $2.47), single $4.25 (rising $5.72, flat $1.52). Split adds ~$0.9/sh, $0.70 of it from Tydal.
